title: Gate clauses
statement: Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input variables, and let $i$ be one of its gate positions. The gate clauses at $i$ are the following list of terms on the $n$ input variables and one variable for each gate: for an input gate, the two terms pairing the gate variable with the input variable using opposite required signs; for a constant gate, the single literal requiring the gate variable to have the sign associated to that Boolean value; for a negation gate, the two terms pairing the gate variable with its source gate using matching signs; for a conjunction gate, two terms pairing the positive gate literal with each negative source literal, followed by a term pairing the negative gate literal with the positive source literals (with only one source literal when both inputs are the same gate); and for a disjunction gate, the corresponding two terms pairing the negative gate literal with each positive source literal, followed by a term pairing the positive gate literal with the negative source literals (again using only one source literal when both inputs are the same gate).
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $n$ of input variables
